findings.title: `definition` binding in the resume paths of `run()` is unconfirmed
findings.description: `run()` now calls `_locked(definition, ...)` in the `--resume` branch and in the implicit-resume branch. In those branches `pipeline` is `None` and the pipeline name comes from `state.pipeline` or `match.pipeline`. The diff doesn't show where `definition` is assigned, so it may be the wrong pipeline, or unbound, when resuming. That would make `pipeline_mutates` decide on the wrong pipeline or raise `NameError`. `test_a_plain_resume_of_a_paused_run_with_the_lock_held_exits_2` mocks the state manager, so it covers the lock but not whether `definition` is correct. Confirm that `definition` is loaded from `state.pipeline` (or `match.pipeline`) before `_locked` is called, and add a test that asserts this.

findings.title: Atomic report write leaks temp files on failure
findings.description: `NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` is followed by `temp.replace(target)`. If `handle.write` or `replace` raises `OSError`, the `.name.xxxx` temp file stays in the runs directory. The existing test `test_a_failed_write_keeps_the_previous_report_and_logs_error` exercises exactly this path and never checks for leftovers. Repeated per-item rewrites, which this slice adds, can make the leak accumulate on a full disk. Unlink the temp file in the `except` path, and assert the directory is clean in the test.

findings.title: `Any`-typed cf client and a circular import across the CLI boundary
findings.description: `resume_item`, `_resume_locked`, `_select_item`, `_open_dependencies` and `_git_precondition` all take `cf_client: Any`, even though `CfClientProtocol` already exists in `branch_ops` and is used for `read_integration_target`. This hides contract errors under strict pyright and breaks the "program to interfaces" rule. Type these parameters with the protocol, extended with `list_slices` and `list_tasks` if needed.

findings.title: `run_item.py` imports private functions from `run.py` at call time
findings.description: `run.py` imports `run_item`, and `run_item` imports `_apply_param_overrides` and `_run_pipeline_sdk` back from `run.py`. The import sits inside the function and carries `pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]`. This is a dependency cycle. Either pass the runner and param parser in as arguments from `run.py`, or move the shared helpers into a module that both files import.

findings.title: Blanket `OSError` handler can mislabel unrelated failures
findings.description: `except OSError` returns "cannot write the batch report" and relies on `batch_report` having already logged the failure. Any `OSError` raised elsewhere under the lock produces that same message and is not logged here. Examples are state loading, the `Path.open` call, or a git or file operation in `restore_target`. Narrow the catch to the report-write call, or log with `_logger.exception` before returning HALTED.

findings.title: Lines over the 88-character limit and `# type: ignore` use in strict tests
findings.description:
Several new lines exceed 88 characters.
- Source: the `_write_each_report` signature, the `_not_ready_reason` signature in `sources.py`, a long line in `run_lock._step_mutates`, and the `rerun.replace(...)` line in `item_resume._resume_locked`.
- Tests: many long lines in the new test files.
- Strict-typing gaps in tests: `test_run_lock_cli.py` and `test_item_resume_validation.py` rely on `# type: ignore[attr-defined]`. Helpers such as `_fresh_p6() -> object` and `body_runner` are untyped, which undermines the strict-pyright-on-tests rule.

Run `ruff format` and type the helpers. For example, return `Result` from `_fresh_p6` and return `BodyRunner` from `body_runner`.

findings.title: `ItemRerun.replace` and `list_tasks` fail with generic errors on missing data
findings.description: `next(...)` without a default in `ItemRerun.replace` raises a bare `StopIteration` if the index is missing from the report. Inside a coroutine, that surfaces as `RuntimeError`. In `ContextForgeClient.list_tasks`, `e["completed"]` and `e["total"]` raise `KeyError` against an older cf that lacks those fields. Failing loudly is correct per project rules, but a message that names the missing item or field would be easier to act on.

findings.title: File and function size drift
findings.description: `executor.py` is well over the ~300-line guideline and keeps growing. `_execute_each_step` is now long, and two loop entry points repeat the `_loop_accept_decision_result` guard. `item_resume.py` is also slightly over the limit. Consider extracting the each-step report and flag logic into its own module in a follow-up.

findings.title: Strengths
findings.description:
- The reserved param keys are defined once in `control_params.py` and enforced at the CLI, in the loader and in `item_params`.
- The run lock is non-blocking and OS-released, with explicit exit codes.
- `report.json` has a schema version and explicit load errors.
- Failure modes are logged and tested: lock held, git-dir failure, unopenable lock file, failed report write, halted git state.
- No credentials or database access were introduced.
